# A test that asserts a wall-clock limit runs alone, in its own isolated collection, and a guard test fails when one does not
<!-- GENERATED from the Phrase Board (issue #417, sha256:703793fedbc0bd6f63427701d07bea3cab54a7f82de16a7ea7d4c8930c249a90). Do not edit this file: edit the issue. -->


- **Status:** Ready
- **Shape:** Story
- **Type:** bug
- **Repository:** avowry (tests/Avowry.Acceptance.Tests)
- **Source:** issue 417 (card 369 retro, Decider D247) and the retros of cards 368, 369 and 418: the timing test failed in the full gate of three cards in a row; ranked next by the card 418 retro. REVISED on 2026-11-11 after the architect's slice and a committed measurement (.mob/records/417/measure-baseline/): the first version of this card (put five more bench classes into the "Bench processes" collection, kept in ready-body-v1.md) was estimated to run the one lane at 16 to 27 minutes against the fixed 15 minute ceiling, and three of the five classes cannot collide with the failing test at all.
- **Depends on:** none
- **Story:** As Dana, I want the release gate's full test run to pass on its first attempt, so that the first preview I am waiting for is not delayed by a ten-minute rerun on every card.
- **Consumer value:** the gate stops costing a ten-minute rerun per card (cards 368, 369 and 418 each paid one), so the publish chain that delivers Dana's first preview is not held up by a test that passes alone in 9 seconds.
- **What the measurement showed (one full acceptance run alone, 10 minutes 10 seconds, 455 tests, toolchain stamp unchanged):** test time per class (under the run's own parallel load): CSharpBaselineAcceptance 518 s, PhraseExecutedOutcomesAcceptance 444 s, PhraseEndpointExecutedOutcomes 147 s, PrivateHoldoutResults 72 s, against the lane today (BenchmarkHarnessAcceptance 217 s, BenchRowsHoldNoFolderPath 72 s, NewBenchRowsCarryNoReply 48 s and the two Restored classes): joining the five classes would add about 20 minutes of test time to the one lane; the only test in the whole project that asserts a wall-clock limit is the timing test (BenchmarkHarnessAcceptance.cs line 48, with the 20 second cancellation of RunBenchmarkArm at line 1453); in the measured run it started at 166 seconds and nothing else was running beside it, and it took 24 seconds for its two arms (the C# arm starts a build-capable `dotnet run`).
- **Definition:** a test class "asserts a wall-clock limit" when, with comments and string contents blanked, its code compares a Stopwatch's or a timer's `Elapsed` or `TotalSeconds` or `TotalMilliseconds` with a limit using `<` or `<=`, or creates a `CancellationTokenSource` with a `TimeSpan.FromSeconds(` or `TimeSpan.FromMilliseconds(` argument and uses its token to fail a test with a "did not finish within" message. Such a class must carry exactly `[Collection("Isolated timing")]`, and one `[CollectionDefinition("Isolated timing", DisableParallelization = true)]` exists in the project: xunit then runs that collection after the parallel collections have finished, with nothing else running.
- **Scenarios:**
  - **Scenario: [Z] no class asserts a wall-clock limit.** Given sources where no class does; When the guard runs; Then it lists nothing.
  - **Scenario: [O][E] one class does and lacks the collection.** Given one class that compares `Elapsed` with a limit, no attribute; When Dana runs the guard; Then the command exits non-zero and names that file and class.
  - **Scenario: [M] today's tree.** Given the repository as it is today; When the guard runs with its Pending trait removed; Then it fails and names exactly BenchmarkHarnessAcceptance (the class that holds the timing test), one line.
  - **Scenario: [B] near misses.** Given classes that mention `Elapsed` only in a comment or a string, that use a TimeSpan limit for a process timeout argument without asserting wall-clock time (the `--timeout-ms` argument, a `WaitForExitAsync` limit in a helper), or that carry a different collection name (`"Isolated Timing"`, `"Bench processes"`); When the guard runs; Then the first two kinds are not named and the last kind is.
  - **Scenario: [I] the interface.** Given the timing test moved into its own class `BenchTimeoutIsolation` with the collection and its helpers; When `dotnet test Avowry.sln --filter "Status!=Pending"` runs alone; Then the timing test passes in the full run and the trx shows that no other class overlapped it; and the guard's own file is not named and `GeneratedApiSourceScan.Guard_checked_set_of_process_start_callers` and `NoBlockingProcessWaits` still pass.
  - **Scenario: [S] a plain run.** Given the gate's full run alone twice in a fresh clone; When it finishes; Then both exit 0, each within the fixed ceiling of 15 minutes of acceptance time (today about 10; the isolated collection adds about 25 seconds), and the committed outputs show the duration and the timing test's result.
- **Acceptance criteria (Given/When/Then; at most 3, each failing on partial work):**
  1. **The guard exists and is offline and build-free.** The new file (Slice 417) scans `tests/Avowry.Acceptance.Tests/**/*.cs` as text with no build and no process, applies the definition above (the blanker handles verbatim, interpolated and raw string literals, several classes in one file and a partial class split across files), requires the exact collection name, names each offender, and carries fixture tests for every row of the near-miss scenario; its live-tree test is Pending in the red and fails by assertion naming BenchmarkHarnessAcceptance.
  2. **The timing test runs alone.** The timing test and its helpers (`RunBenchmarkArm`, `WriteIgnoringModelTree` and whatever only it uses) live in a new class `BenchTimeoutIsolation` carrying `[Collection("Isolated timing")]`; one `CollectionDefinition` with `DisableParallelization = true` exists; BenchmarkHarnessAcceptance keeps every other test and its `"Bench processes"` collection; the test's body and its 20 second limits are unchanged; the guard's live-tree test has no Pending trait and passes.
  3. **The full gate passes within the ceiling.** Two full runs alone of `dotnet test Avowry.sln --filter "Status!=Pending"` on the final head in a fresh clone, each with the toolchain stamp (D251) before and after, both exit 0; the committed outputs (the summary with the acceptance duration under 15 minutes, a console log at normal verbosity or a trx class summary that shows the timing test's result, and the sign-off's raw output file) are in the records before the sign-off is accepted.
- **ZOMBIES:** Z no offender; O one offender; M today's tree and the helper set that moves with the test; B near misses (comment, string, a process timeout argument, a wrong collection name); I the collection definition and the interface between the moved test and its helpers; E the guard names the offender; S two clean full runs.
- **Rulings (facilitator, 2026-11-11):** (1) this revised card replaces the first version after the measurement; the revised design is put to a new Decider (D253) before the slice is used; (2) the ceiling stays FIXED at 15 minutes of acceptance time per full run, verified from committed outputs (D252's condition keeps its force); (3) the five-class collection of the first version is not done: a later card may revisit it if a second class ever fails under load; (4) the D247 entry is unchanged by this card; its trial counter and wording are reviewed in the retro; (5) the Phrase classes that start only the no-build Avowry.Bench tool cannot collide on the C# tool's folder and stay as they are; (6) persona Dana; size S; D251 applies to every gate and the sign-off; the account-name rule (stricter) is in every brief.
- **Not in this card:** changing the 20 second limits; making the C# arm use `--no-build`; serialising other classes; changing LlmCustomerCheck's own collection; any production code.
- **Size:** S
